Personality: Ratagost is an outlier among the lords of Sturgia; lacking the characteristic ferocity and recklessness of the northmen, he is known instead for his mercy and caution. On the battlefield, he shows a marked inclination to avoid open combat, his lack of boldness leading him to avert direct clashes through superior tactical deployment and reconnaissance intelligence rather than charging at the vanguard. Kind-hearted by nature, he often feels pity for the common folk and prisoners of war, which makes him stand out awkwardly within the martial Vyroving clan. Confronted with the overbearing and cruel rule of clan chief Vashorki, Ratagost conducts himself submissively, accustomed to keeping silent beneath a heavy hand. Far from lacking ability, his consummate horsemanship and skill with polearms prove him a capable warrior, yet he prefers to use his wisdom to preserve himself and his family, playing the part of a clear-eyed and low-key caretaker amid turbulent politics.
Background: Ratagost hails from the prominent Vyroving clan of Sturgia and currently resides at the family seat of Ov Castle. As a loyal vassal of Grand Prince Raganvad, he has witnessed Sturgia's turbulent transformation from a tribal confederation into a hereditary principality. Although his house is led by the ruthless and domineering Vashorki, Ratagost retains an important standing within the clan through his mastery of tactics and leadership. Father to four children—Yachana, Milanka, Vilina, and Bovan—he carefully maintains his allegiance to Raganvad in a political climate where the northern boyars widely resent monarchical centralization and the seeds of rebellion lie buried deep. Throughout his life, he has sought to balance oppressive rule within his clan against the threat of war from without, dedicating himself to carving out a path of survival sustained by caution and wisdom for his children across a northern land rife with intrigue and violence.
